title: Runtime, editor and diagnostics capability comparison

classification_meanings.explicit_policy: An explicit declaration or settled product decision, including declared host-only capability.
classification_meanings.explicit_mechanism: Different native owners implement equivalent product intent.
classification_meanings.implementation_constraint: An identified OS/dependency/API constraint; no universal technical impossibility is inferred beyond it.
classification_meanings.observed_defect: Confirmed actionable behavior within the report’s explicit executed/source-derived evidence boundary.
classification_meanings.observed_limit: Measured or source-reviewed limit, coverage gap, or weaker evidence that is not a new confirmed defect.
classification_meanings.unknown_intent: Difference observed, but the product/privacy obligation needed to call it a defect is unestablished.
classification_meanings.refuted_or_demoted: Candidate is excluded from confirmed findings after whole-owner/context countercheck.

scope_register.macos: Owned remap install/provision/approval; WebView/editors; diagnostics/crash/export. Ollama is a source-compared counterpart, not the Mac runtime audit subject.
scope_register.linux: Managed Ollama; in-process LGI/WebKit editors; diagnostics/crash/export.

evidence_boundary: A revision-pinned comparison from nine bounded audit reports and coordinator adjudications. No real native three-OS receiving or all-product parity certification. Reports may contain provisional wording; explicit adjudications below govern excluded candidates.

adjudications.summary: Valid unlimited numeric 0 is serialized by all three hosts but ms || defaultMs displays the positive default. One shared root, not three findings.

Actual refused CAS/write plus independent shortcut close destroys attempted draft on Mac reopen. Windows host hardcodes menu mode; Linux close is separately a no-op. Loud Mac refusal does not restore the draft.

Durable bytes saved, live reload refused, prior engine retained, and actual Config error is loud. saved=true/bridge-alert count alone does not establish silent save loss; exclude the provisional cohort claim from confirmed findings.

Unanswered logical timeout with pending native child is not physical-done success or proof consent was withdrawn. Original EX lifecycle lock fences publication; asserted overlap consequence was not proved.

capabilities.title: Native browser and message ownership

behavior.windows: WebView2/COM hosts, native fallback forms, retained subscriptions and per-session epochs.
behavior.macos: Hammerspoon hs.webview/WKWebView; controller pool and deferred close ownership.
behavior.linux: GTK/WebKit2GTK through LGI inside the daemon; native signals and page epochs. No editor worker/socket protocol.

capabilities.rationale: Equivalent editor/diagnostics capabilities use distinct native APIs. No actual native browser receiving, GUI destruction or three-OS lifecycle certification was performed.

capabilities.title: Personal hotstrings and personal-information editing

behavior.windows: Structured personal TOML editor, category settings and action picker through WebView/native owners.
behavior.macos: Hotstring editor, personal-information form, metadata settings and action picker through their own owners.
behavior.linux: Structured personal.toml editor plus personal_info.toml field form; other TOMLs retain their own owners.

capabilities.rationale: Missing same-named modules do not establish a feature gap. These are structured forms, not evidence of a universal arbitrary-TOML editor requirement.

capabilities.title: A universal raw TOML editor

behavior.windows: No general capability inferred from the personal editor name.
behavior.macos: Dedicated forms are present; a universal text editor is not established.
behavior.linux: No personal_toml_editor registry entry; dedicated hotstring and information editors exist.

capabilities.rationale: A product requirement for identical generic text editing was not found. Do not classify absence of a matching API/module name as a confirmed defect.

capabilities.title: Unlimited zero delay in category/section controls

behavior.windows: Native state preserves numeric 0 and engine unlimited semantics; shared input displays positive default.
behavior.macos: State builder preserves effective 0 and delay_unlimited semantics; same shared renderer substitutes default.
behavior.linux: fields_for preserves numeric 0; same shared renderer substitutes default.

capabilities.rationale: WVB-002 is one shared all-OS cause: bindDelay assigns ms || defaultMs, conflating valid unlimited 0 with absence. It is not an intentional platform delay difference.

capabilities.title: Personal-editor refused-save feedback

behavior.windows: WVB-001: double quoting a complete JSON literal generates invalid failure-toast JavaScript; paused save can retain the optimistic Saved indication. Ordinary commit failure has a separate notifier.
behavior.macos: Hotstring/configuration editors observe failure and notify; action-picker initialization has a separate delivery gap.
behavior.linux: Actual Config failure logs remain relevant even when bridge return says saved; see demoted LVB-002 below.

capabilities.rationale: WVB-001 concerns failure visibility. A transport submission or native script completion is not a JavaScript application acknowledgement; loud sibling failure paths must be included before claiming silence.

capabilities.title: Action-picker initial data delivery

behavior.windows: WebView_RunScriptAsync observes native submission/completion; actual WebView2 receiving remains unexecuted.
behavior.macos: MVB-001: actual picker swallows encoding/evaluation exceptions and installs no completion observer; page remains open without a central failure.
behavior.linux: Manager/bridge native-currentness and failure/debt controls exercised through native-shaped ports.

capabilities.rationale: The confirmed Mac root rests on swallowed exceptions, not an assumption that Hammerspoon normally returns false/nil or that native stderr is silent. No corresponding Windows/Linux defect was established.

capabilities.title: Shortcut save followed by automatic close

behavior.windows: Actual host hardcodes open_mode=menu; shared shortcut automatic-close branch is unreachable through this owner.
behavior.macos: MVB-002: actual shortcut mode emits save then independent close; CAS/write refusal is loud, but host requests deletion and actual reopen loses the attempted draft.
behavior.linux: Shortcut branch is reachable, but LVB-001 close command is a no-op and never invokes the trusted close capability; this does not prove Mac-style draft destruction.

capabilities.rationale: One shared frontend branch has different reachable host consequences. MVB-002 is refused-save draft preservation, not merely an optimistic toast. LVB-001 is missing close effect; neither is duplicated onto Windows.

capabilities.title: Durable save versus live reload

behavior.windows: Exact opening source and acknowledged write/live publication are owned by the native commit path.
behavior.macos: Actual editor checks reload commitment and notifies refusal while retaining prior live state.
behavior.linux: LVB-002 is DEMOTED: private bytes are saved durably while reload refuses and engine generation stays unchanged; actual Config emits a loud error.

capabilities.rationale: A saved durable file and failed live application are separate facts. saved=true plus bridge alerts=0 alone does not establish a silent lost save when the actual lower owner reports refusal. Candidate receipt handling remains a review observation, not a confirmed new root.

capabilities.title: Editor focus and native fallback behavior

behavior.windows: window_focus is explicitly ignored; named launchers provide native AHK form/ListBox fallbacks.
behavior.macos: Editor focus guard and host-specific unavailable/error behavior.
behavior.linux: Input capture gate owns editor focus; native runtime absence/headless state refuses construction.

capabilities.rationale: Windows focus no-op and fallback promises are explicit host behavior. Equivalent pixel styling or identical focus/capture internals are not a shared requirement established here.

capabilities.title: Managed Ollama selection and consent

behavior.windows: Managed pinned runtime under LocalAppData/Ergopti/ollama; own port 11435, reject ambient stock 11434. Silent startup does not grant install/pull consent.
behavior.macos: Managed-runtime-only counterpart is source-compared by sibling reports; this campaign Mac runtime audit primarily covers remap, not full Ollama bootstrap.
behavior.linux: Per-user XDG version/architecture/digest target, official pinned archive and explicit repair consent; own port 11435, reject stock 11434.

capabilities.rationale: PIN/own-runtime-only and explicit install consent are settled policy. Differing roots/security APIs are mechanisms, not missing parity. Full Mac/Windows/Linux inference installation was not run.

capabilities.title: Managed Ollama status after first installation

behavior.windows: Current pinned bootstrap admission differs from cheap advisory directory presence; old-version display intent remains unestablished.
behavior.macos: Ollama candidate/hint lookup is a source counterpart, not a newly qualified native install.
behavior.linux: LRT-001: browser caches missing-ancestor resolver; independent installer creates those parents, leaving empty-inventory browser state absent until observer reset.

capabilities.rationale: Linux immutable ancestry checks are correct within an operation; lifetime reuse across the separate installation causes stale observer state. Do not infer matching sibling defects from similar labels.

capabilities.title: Remap/tap-hold runtime architecture

behavior.windows: Native AHK remap/tap-hold/input owners; no Karabiner/DriverKit package.
behavior.macos: Owned Karabiner fork, Core/Console and pqrs VirtualHIDDevice; native approval and capture admission.
behavior.linux: Native Lua tap-hold engine with evdev capture and uinput; no Karabiner dependency.

capabilities.rationale: Equivalent input intent uses OS-specific mechanisms. DriverKit, launchd and Mac approval panes have no corresponding dependency on Windows/Linux. Counterpart source review is not native input qualification.

capabilities.title: Runtime installation authority and approval

behavior.windows: Windows job/handle/DACL and input-hook lifecycles require native qualification.
behavior.macos: Protected install needs administrator authority, followed by OS driver approval. Explicit Mac-only install/approval rows; Developer ID remains deferred by decision.
behavior.linux: Permission setup configures the explicit/local graphical UID for input/uinput and udev/module rules.

capabilities.rationale: Native permission/security systems differ. The Mac-only menu declaration is explicit; installing the Mac dependency on other OS is not owed parity. No privileged operation ran in this campaign.

capabilities.title: Approval observation deadline and Settings receipt

behavior.windows: No DriverKit approval observer counterpart.
behavior.macos: MRT-001 counts poll intervals rather than elapsed task/timer time; MRT-006 accepts false Settings-open result because only pcall status is checked.
behavior.linux: No DriverKit approval observer counterpart.

capabilities.rationale: Mac approval is inherently platform-specific; truthful opening failure and bounded observation remain ordinary product requirements. Linux libuv timing qualifies the scaled experiment only, not Mac native latency.

capabilities.title: Runtime command deadline admission

behavior.windows: Managed bootstrap retains native task/file debt; actual AHK timer/NTFS behavior was not executed.
behavior.macos: MRT-002: bounded runner ignores Timer.after committed=false and can leave a started install without a deadline/terminal result.
behavior.linux: Managed repair owns budget plus finite/service process capabilities; no same runtime-command defect retained.

capabilities.rationale: An allocated handle is not an armed deadline. This Mac runtime join and Linux diagnostics LDG-003 have related receipt themes but distinct owners and regressions.

capabilities.title: Runtime receipt and post-publication recovery

behavior.windows: Exact source/archive/WAL/native ownership paths reviewed; interrupted root-marker recovery remains an unconfirmed expectation.
behavior.macos: MRT-003: Lua cache accepts receipt suffixes rejected by exact Swift guard. MRT-004: exposed first-install retry cannot repair already-present Runtime after service provisioning failure.
behavior.linux: No-replace publication and captured cleanup preserve foreign/late-published trees; old-pin reclamation and runtime purge product policy remain unknown.

capabilities.rationale: Mac cache/install consistency and recoverable provisioning are confirmed within stated source/model boundaries. Existing-tree refusal must stay; a recovery route must not blindly overwrite unknown/live state.

capabilities.title: Logical timeout and privileged helper continuation

behavior.windows: Task/receipt cleanup retains native debt and blocks replacements until acknowledgement, source reviewed.
behavior.macos: MRT-005 is NOT confirmed: pending child after logical timeout does not revoke existing consent or prove corruption; original EX lifecycle lock fences publication.
behavior.linux: Cancellation and process-group/close receipts are distinct; uncertain acquisition is not inferred settled.

capabilities.rationale: A signal, unanswered install or cleared logical waiter is not physical completion. Forbidden continuation or bad effect was not established; EX-lock protection refutes the asserted overlapping-publication consequence.

capabilities.title: Application removal versus runtime/model purge

behavior.windows: App uninstall explicitly removes confirmed executable/startup shortcut after parent exit; runtime, models and user config survive. Source checkout uninstall refuses visibly.
behavior.macos: App Trash/termination counterpart is source-compared; remap runtime lifecycle/other-Karabiner restoration has separate explicit ownership.
behavior.linux: App removal is manifest-scoped; no user-facing managed-runtime purge or in-place update transaction established in the audited Ollama call graph.

capabilities.rationale: Windows retention is explicit policy, not a new defect. Whether all platforms should offer a purge-all/old-pin cleanup action is unknown; app removal and runtime removal must not be conflated.

capabilities.title: Quick/extensive checks, page observations and driver suites

behavior.windows: Shared snapshot/probes; guided collection and resident controls explicitly keep native/physical scenarios unqualified or UNRUN.
behavior.macos: Driver-specific quick/extensive probes; installed-page model/synthetic checks remain unqualified.
behavior.linux: Local configuration by default, optional extensive providers; shared model observations remain unqualified.

capabilities.rationale: driver-suites: not_run and installed_page_reported (unqualified) are authority boundaries. A saved archive, page-model PASS or function-existence check does not qualify native driver/install/reload behavior.

capabilities.title: Guided native diagnostic collection

behavior.windows: Declared Windows-only independent collection job/session and bounded receipt-based ZIP; guided scenarios retain explicit unrun/unqualified status.
behavior.macos: Init capability diagnostic_collection=false; ordinary diagnostics still available.
behavior.linux: Init capability diagnostic_collection=false; ordinary diagnostics still available.

capabilities.rationale: The Windows-only collection is an explicit declared asymmetry. No universal native technical impossibility on Mac/Linux was established; absence does not authorize inventing a substitute PASS.

capabilities.title: Diagnostics selected AI backend and off state

behavior.windows: Helpers preserve actual backend and boolean off; non-Ollama local-health checks are unsupported.
behavior.macos: Helpers preserve actual backend/false; schema path gates unsupported backends before local-health request.
behavior.linux: LDG-001 attributes API input to Ollama and probes local Ollama; LDG-002 erases false to nil, rendering Enabled unknown and omitting known off in export.

capabilities.rationale: API is supported by Linux engine; no policy makes local Ollama a proxy for selected remote API health. Known off differs from absent/unavailable. Actual shared model/export replay establishes the display consequence.

capabilities.title: Diagnostics refusal, timeout and cancellation

behavior.windows: Native SetTimer/poll deadlines and owner/session checks are source-reviewed; no Windows timer failure execution.
behavior.macos: Probe watchdog explicitly checks committed receipt; actor/cleanup status remains separate from business result.
behavior.linux: LDG-003 ignores returned unarmed scheduler handle after native allocation/start refusal; configuration stays pending with no remaining timer. Lower scheduler logs the error.

capabilities.rationale: The Linux missing terminal result is not total diagnostic silence or a native memory-exhaustion measurement. Fault seams use faithful return shapes; healthy real timer and actual handle cleanup controls pass.

capabilities.title: HTTP connectivity versus complete provider readiness

behavior.windows: HTTP status can describe endpoint reachability even when optional version/rate-limit fields cannot parse.
behavior.macos: Same bounded endpoint-answer interpretation; no successful inference implied.
behavior.linux: Actual curl exit18/status200 can yield probe ok while transport logs failure; retained as a bounded observation, not a confirmed completeness defect.

capabilities.rationale: Backend answers is weaker than valid complete payload, authenticated provider correctness or model inference. The Linux API-to-Ollama attribution is separately LDG-001. Preserve loud lower-layer errors.

capabilities.title: Approved copy/save/report and opt-in day log

behavior.windows: Closed typed English report; exact host preview; separate redacted day-log slot/cap; no automatic upload.
behavior.macos: Same closed host projection, snapshot-bound redacted day log, save/reveal/browser ordering.
behavior.linux: Same closed projection; real unprivileged native write/close/permission controls refuse incomplete diagnostic saves before reveal.

capabilities.rationale: Raw local snapshot detail is not the shared attachment. Canary controls support bounded policy assertions, not exhaustive privacy certification or actual OS clipboard/browser success.

capabilities.title: Local crash-file privacy policy

behavior.windows: Full error/stack/log/window context locally is explicitly documented; sharing has its separate redacted boundary.
behavior.macos: Raw recognized token/account/path canaries reach local crash JSON; categorical no-personal-data comments conflict with output. Mac local-retention intent is unknown.
behavior.linux: Crash dump captures admitted sink redactor/currentness and redacts before opening/writing; no raw fallback.

capabilities.rationale: These are actual different local policies/mechanisms. Windows raw retention is explicit; Linux is stricter; Mac comment inconsistency is not promoted to an automatic-upload/data-leak finding without policy adjudication.

capabilities.title: Failed crash-worker artifact completeness

behavior.windows: WDG-001, LOW: both PowerShell writers can leave truncated canonical .json after partial write refusal; no OK or saved notification is emitted.
behavior.macos: Create-if-absent writer/retention controls exercised through Linux-backed filesystem port; Darwin physical write/identity behavior unqualified.
behavior.linux: Regular writer/close/path-image receipts and redaction fail closed; no blanket cross-OS crash failure-atomicity claim.

capabilities.rationale: Actual PowerShell/.NET private Linux file-size refusal proves Windows worker mechanism, not a measured Windows disk-full incident. This is failed-artifact cleanup, not false saved success or a privacy leak.

capabilities.title: Platform diagnostics and known gaps

behavior.windows: Native UIA/guided collection available by declaration; unavailable-feature explanation absent and already in prior TODO.
behavior.macos: External AppleEvent transport/permissions differ; manifest unavailable-feature explanation exists.
behavior.linux: X11 detailed app list; Wayland app enumeration omitted with explanation. Portable reveal opens containing directory, not file selection. Unavailable-feature explanation already backlog.

capabilities.rationale: Wayland enumeration and platform transport differ for native reasons. Existing unavailable-feature parity debt is not reissued. Implementing only Windows guided collection is explicit policy, not proof that Mac/Linux are technically incapable.

capabilities.title: Native receiving, memory and performance qualification

behavior.windows: Portable PowerShell/source/JS controls only; no AHK, WebView2, NTFS/ACL/listener or physical driver receiving.
behavior.macos: Lua/native-shaped ports and selected Linux-backed file/timing controls only; no Darwin WebKit, Swift/security/launchd/DriverKit receiving.
behavior.linux: Actual private POSIX/libuv/source/save/HTTP-helper controls; no GTK/WebKit receiving, live managed model, corporate network or physical input.

capabilities.rationale: No native three-OS certification, production latency percentile or steady-state native heap/leak rate follows. Module/test timings and modeled cleanup are not production performance or physical retirement receipts.
